ai.description: *Raorchestes blandus* is a small frog (20–25 mm) with a pale brown dorsum and dark brown lateral bands. It features a distinct white snout tip and granular skin texture with scattered dark spots.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Raorchestes blandus* is best distinguished by its unique, vibrant yellow-orange iris, which contrasts sharply with the dark, mottled brown patterns on its body.
ai.habitat: The Anamalai bush frog inhabits the mid-to-high elevation evergreen forests and shola grasslands of the Western Ghats, typically found at altitudes between 1,000 and 2,000m.
ai.behavior: The Anamalai bush frog is primarily nocturnal, spending its nights perched on leaves where it actively hunts for small insects and other invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes blandus* exhibits direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. It breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs in arboreal microhabitats.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Anamalai Bush Frog is endemic to the Anamalai Hills in the Western Ghats, spanning the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu at elevations between 1,000 and 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Anamalai Bush Frog emits a series of high-pitched, insect-like "tink" calls, typically heard from vegetation within moist evergreen forests.
